rows.stem: PQ is tangent to a circle with centre O. If \(OQ = a\), \(OP = a + 2\) and \(PQ = 2b\), then relation between a and b is
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that Q is the point of contact (OQ a radius, so the right angle is at Q) is shown only in the drawing, which labels OQ = a, OP = a+2 and PQ = 2b. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
Q is the point of contact, so the radius OQ is perpendicular to the tangent PQ, and triangle OQP is right-angled at Q.

\(OP^2 = OQ^2 + PQ^2\): \((a + 2)^2 = a^2 + (2b)^2\), so \(a^2 + 4a + 4 = a^2 + 4b^2\).

That is \(4b^2 = 4a + 4\), or \(b^2 = a + 1\), which is option (D) \(b^2 = a + 1\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(AB \parallel EF\). If AB = 24 cm, EF = 36 cm and DA = 7 cm, then AE equals
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that A lies on DE and B on DF (triangle DEF with AB parallel to its base EF) is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
A lies on DE and B on DF, with \(AB \parallel EF\). So \(\Delta DAB \sim \Delta DEF\) (AA similarity), and \(\dfrac{DA}{DE} = \dfrac{AB}{EF}\).

\(\dfrac{7}{DE} = \dfrac{24}{36} = \dfrac{2}{3}\), so \(DE = 10.5\) cm.

\(AE = DE - DA = 10.5 - 7 = 3.5\) cm, which is option (C) \(3.5\) cm.

rows.subtopic: Nature of Roots and the Discriminant
rows.stem: The value of m for which the quadratic equation \(3x^2 - 7x + m = 0\) has real and equal roots, is
rows.solution:
Real and equal roots need the discriminant to be zero: \((-7)^2 - 4 \times 3 \times m = 0\), that is \(49 - 12m = 0\).

So \(m = \dfrac{49}{12}\), which is option (B) \(\dfrac{49}{12}\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem: Two dice are rolled together. The probability of getting an outcome \((x, y)\) where \(x > y\), is
rows.solution:
Two dice give \(6 \times 6 = 36\) equally likely outcomes.

The outcomes with \(x > y\) are: for \(x = 2\), one (\(y = 1\)); for \(x = 3\), two; for \(x = 4\), three; for \(x = 5\), four; for \(x = 6\), five. That is \(1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15\) outcomes.

\(P(x > y) = \dfrac{15}{36} = \dfrac{5}{12}\), which is option (A) \(\dfrac{5}{12}\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: In the given figure, point D divides the side BC of \(\Delta ABC\) in the ratio \(1 : 2\). Find length AD.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the coordinates A(1, 5), B(-2, 1) and C(4, 2) are printed only in the drawing of triangle ABC with D on BC. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
From the figure, \(A(1, 5)\), \(B(-2, 1)\) and \(C(4, 2)\). D divides BC in the ratio \(1 : 2\), so by the section formula

\(D = \left(\dfrac{1 \times 4 + 2 \times (-2)}{1 + 2}, \dfrac{1 \times 2 + 2 \times 1}{1 + 2}\right) = \left(0, \dfrac{4}{3}\right)\).

\(AD = \sqrt{(1 - 0)^2 + \left(5 - \dfrac{4}{3}\right)^2} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{121}{9}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{130}{9}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{130}}{3}\) units.

rows.subtopic: Irrational Numbers and Proof by Contradiction
rows.stem: Prove that \(14 - 2\sqrt{3}\) is an irrational number, given that \(\sqrt{3}\) is irrational.
rows.solution:
Suppose, to the contrary, that \(14 - 2\sqrt{3}\) is rational. Then \(14 - 2\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{a}{b}\), where a and b are integers and \(b \neq 0\).

Rearranging, \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{14b - a}{2b}\). The right side is a ratio of integers, so it is rational; but \(\sqrt{3}\) is irrational. This is a contradiction.

So the assumption is wrong, and \(14 - 2\sqrt{3}\) is irrational.

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem: Use graphical method to solve the system of linear equations : \(x = -3\) and \(5x - 2y = -5\).
rows.solution:
\(x = -3\) is the vertical line through \((-3, 0)\), parallel to the y-axis.

Points on \(5x - 2y = -5\), that is \(y = \dfrac{5x + 5}{2}\):

| \(x\) | \(-1\) | 1 | \(-3\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 0 | 5 | \(-5\) |

Plot these points and draw the line through them, and draw the line \(x = -3\) on the same axes. The two lines meet at \((-3, -5)\).

The solution is \(x = -3\), \(y = -5\). (Check: \(5(-3) - 2(-5) = -15 + 10 = -5\).)

rows.stem: A chord of a circle, of radius 14 cm, subtends an angle of \(60^\circ\) at the centre. Find the area of the smaller sector and perimeter of the smaller segment.
rows.solution:
Let the chord be AB and the centre O. \(OA = OB = 14\) cm and \(\angle AOB = 60^\circ\), so triangle OAB is isosceles with base angles \(60^\circ\) each: it is equilateral, and \(AB = 14\) cm.

Area of the smaller sector \(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 14 = \dfrac{308}{3}\ \text{cm}^2 \approx 102.67\ \text{cm}^2\).

Length of the minor arc \(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 = \dfrac{44}{3}\) cm.

The smaller segment is bounded by the chord and the minor arc, so its perimeter \(= 14 + \dfrac{44}{3} = \dfrac{86}{3}\) cm \(\approx 28.67\) cm.

rows.stem:
The mean of the following distribution is 53. Find the missing frequency p.

| **Class Interval** | 0 – 20 | 20 – 40 | 40 – 60 | 60 – 80 | 80 – 100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Frequency** | 12 | 15 | p | 28 | 13 |

Hence, find mode of the distribution.

rows.solution:
The mid-values go up in steps of 10, so each class has width 10 and runs 5 either side of its mid-value.

| Mid-value | Class Interval | f | cf |
|---|---|---|---|
| 115 | 110 – 120 | 12 | 12 |
| 125 | 120 – 130 | 15 | 27 |
| 135 | 130 – 140 | 20 | 47 |
| 145 | 140 – 150 | 16 | 63 |
| 155 | 150 – 160 | 10 | 73 |
| 165 | 160 – 170 | 16 | 89 |
| 175 | 170 – 180 | 11 | 100 |

\(\dfrac{N}{2} = \dfrac{100}{2} = 50\). The first cumulative frequency above 50 is 63, so the median class is 140-150, with \(l = 140\), \(cf = 47\), \(f = 16\), \(h = 10\).

Median \(= 140 + \dfrac{50 - 47}{16} \times 10 = 140 + 1.875 = 141.875\), that is \(\dfrac{1135}{8}\).

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: Two water taps together can fill a tank in \(8\dfrac{8}{9}\) hours. The tap of larger diameter takes 4 hours less than the smaller one to fill the tank separately. Find the time in which each tap can separately fill the tank.
rows.solution:
Let the tap of smaller diameter take x hours to fill the tank alone. The larger tap then takes \((x - 4)\) hours.

In one hour the two taps fill \(\dfrac{1}{x}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{x - 4}\) of the tank. Together they take \(8\dfrac{8}{9} = \dfrac{80}{9}\) hours, so they fill \(\dfrac{9}{80}\) of it in an hour:

\(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x - 4} = \dfrac{9}{80}\).

\(80(x - 4 + x) = 9x(x - 4)\), so \(160x - 320 = 9x^2 - 36x\), that is \(9x^2 - 196x + 320 = 0\).

\((x - 20)(9x - 16) = 0\), so \(x = 20\) or \(x = \dfrac{16}{9}\).

For \(x = \dfrac{16}{9}\) the larger tap's time \(x - 4\) would be negative, so this root is rejected, and \(x = 20\).

The tap of smaller diameter fills the tank in 20 hours and the tap of larger diameter in 16 hours. (Check: \(\dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{4 + 5}{80} = \dfrac{9}{80}\).)
